questions.q: List any four key words from the poem "olar vk;k" that are explained in the NCERT vocabulary section ('kCnkFkZ vkSj fVIi.kh').
questions.a:
Correct answer: Any four from: oqQÅduk, pqjeqjk,, r#oj, fiQjdh, enueghuk, ngj&ngj, ngduk, <kd, uanu ou, eèkqeLr, fid, ux.;.  
A wrong answer (e.g., listing words not in the vocabulary list like "olar" or "vk;k") reveals the student cannot distinguish between the poet’s general vocabulary and the specific terms the textbook highlights for contextual study. This suggests they are not using the NCERT apparatus as a study tool.

questions.q: Explain the difference between the literal meaning of "fiQjdh" and its contextual meaning in the line "f[kyh gqbZ gok vkbZ] fiQjdh&lh vkbZ] pyh xbZ" from "olar vk;k".
questions.a:
Correct answer: Literally, "fiQjdh" means "evening" or "twilight". Contextually, paired with "fiQjdh&lh" (lingering evening), it conveys a reluctant, heavy dusk that drags its feet — the "gok" (cow) has returned, the "lh" (dust) has settled, yet the evening refuses to end, mirroring the poet’s sense of time stretching painfully.  
A wrong answer that only gives the dictionary meaning shows the student treats vocabulary as static definitions. They miss how the compound "fiQjdh&lh" and the verb "pyh xbZ" (slipped away) personify time as a weary entity, which is central to the poem’s mood of helplessness.

questions.q: In the poem "rksM+ks", the word "O;kih" appears in the line "vius eu osQ eSnkuksa ij O;kih oSQlh Åc gS". Use "O;kih" in an original sentence that captures its poetic connotation of being deeply, almost painfully, rooted.
questions.a:
Correct answer: "The old banyan tree stood O;kih in the courtyard, its roots embracing the earth so tightly that no storm could dislodge it — a silent witness to generations."  
A wrong answer like "The plant is O;kih in the pot" treats it as a simple botanical term ("firmly fixed"). The student fails to grasp that in the poem, "O;kih" describes the heart’s memories (eSnkuksa) as immovable, almost burdensome, fixtures — the connotation is emotional weight, not physical stability.

questions.q: Compare how the words "ngj&ngj" (in "olar vk;k") and "ux.;" (in the same poem) contribute to the portrayal of time’s passage. Use specific lines as evidence.
questions.a:
Correct answer: "ngj&ngj" (slowly, gradually) appears in "ngj&ngj ngosaQxs dgha <kd osQ taxy vke ckSj vkosaxs" — it depicts time as a creeping, almost imperceptible thief that steals youth drop by drop. "ux.;" (sudden, unexpected) appears in "vkt osQ ux.; fnu tkuw¡xk" — it marks the shocking moment when the inevitable (old age/death) finally announces itself. Together, they frame time as a dual process: a long, quiet erosion followed by a sudden, irreversible arrival.  
A wrong answer that defines them only as "slowly" and "suddenly" misses the structural contrast: the poem moves from the prolonged agony of waiting (ngj&ngj) to the blunt finality of the end (ux.;). This contrast is the poem’s temporal architecture.

questions.q: Which single word from the combined vocabulary list of both poems do you think most powerfully conveys the central theme of "the inevitability of aging and the futility of resistance"? Justify your choice with reference to at least two lines.
questions.a:
Correct answer (example): "rksM+ks" (from the poem "rksM+ks"). The repeated refrain "rksM+ks rksM+ks rksM+ks" is a command to pile up — wood, fire, memories, even the heart’s ashes. It appears in "lc [ksr cukdj NksM+ks" (make a pyre and pile it up) and "xksM+ks xksM+ks xksM+ks" (burn, burn, burn). The word embodies the frantic, repetitive human attempt to build meaning against entropy, yet the imperative tone reveals desperation, not control.  
A wrong answer choosing a descriptive word like "fiQjdh" or "enueghuk" shows the student picks imagery over thematic function. They haven’t learned to ask: "Which word *performs* the theme?" The refrain "rksM+ks" is a verb of action that becomes a ritual of surrender.

questions.q: Write a two-line poem (in Hindi or English) using at least three words from the NCERT vocabulary list, preserving the melancholic, reflective mood of Jagjit Singh’s poems.
questions.a:
Expected criteria: The poem must use three vocabulary words (e.g., ngj&ngj, ux.;, O;kih) naturally, not forced. The mood should be contemplative, dealing with time/memory. Example: "ngj&ngj beet gayi raat, ux.; aayi subah ki khabar / O;kih yaadein ab bhi hain, jaise koi purana shajar."  
A poor answer that merely strings words together ("ngj&ngj ux.; O;kih hain") reveals the student sees vocabulary as isolated tokens. They haven’t internalized that these words carry emotional atmospheres that must be woven into a coherent voice.
